currentFocus: S285 ran the full /arc as one continuous mission on a board S284 had largely cleared. Rather than manufacture work, it verified the thin carry list against LIVE code (the Franchise Architect 301 is live: /games/vaultspark-football-gm/ -> 301 -> /games/franchise-architect/, new slug 200; the S282 verify names a pruned run) and followed the one real CI signal: the CI Status Beacon had gone red twice on gh HTTP 503, a transient GitHub outage. A health beacon that reports the repo unhealthy on the provider own weather is the CANON-031 lie applied to CI. Root-fix (D-S285.1): build-ci-status-beacon.mjs gained isTransientGhError() + retry-with-backoff + an honest-dark degrade (transient exhaustion preserves last-known-good + exits 0; real errors still surface). The check-every-failure-mode sweep found the identical class in fetch-rum-from-r2.mjs (exit 1 on transient R2 5xx) and fixed it the same way, keeping AccessDenied a hard-fail so the standing token-scope blocker stays visible. Second-order: check-ci-publisher-resilience.mjs makes unattended-publisher transient-degrade a standing contract (clean 0/27, self-test with teeth), sibling to check-build-step-resilience. build:check 215/215 EXIT 0, doctor 15/15 blockingFailing 0, scan-secrets 0.
publicNote: This update was about making it easier to see what we ship. Our changelog is now searchable and filterable by year, every entry has its own shareable link, and clicking the latest line on the homepage takes you straight to that update. The homepage live-activity line now reads in plain language instead of developer shorthand. We also renamed our football game from VaultSpark Football GM to Franchise Architect — a cleaner name we can grow across every sport — and the old links redirect to the new ones automatically. Retired names now get a public tombstone pointing to what they became, so our history stays honest. And the changelog will now stay current going forward. PREVIOUS: This session was a clean recovery. A previous automated work session had finished six behind-the-scenes repairs but was cut off before saving them; we verified each repair actually worked rather than taking the earlier session's word for it, caught and fixed one mistake it had left behind, and saved everything as one clearly-labelled checkpoint.
